THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR  ORAL JUDGMENT

This Miscellaneous Second Appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 28.04.2018 passed in R.A.No.330/2017 on the file of I Additional District & Sessions Judge, Tumakuru and the judgment and award dated 13.10.2014 passed in LAC No.208/2006 on the file of Senior Civil Judge, Gubbi, seeking enhancement of compensation praying to award the compensation of Rs.6,000/- per gunta.
2.

entities.text: I Additional District & Sessions Judge, Tumakuru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claimant's land bearing Sy.No.125 measuring 05 acre 15 guntas of land situated at Kodiyala Village, Gubbi Taluk, Tumakuru District was acquired for the project of formation of the Hemavathi Canal under preliminary notification dated 09.08.1990 and final notification dated 22.08.1991.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer (SLAO) has NC: 2024:KHC:44943 determined compensation of Rs.450/- per gunta.
The Reference Court has enhanced the compensation to Rs.1,050/- per gunta.
3. Being aggrieved by this, the appellant/claimant has preferred regular appeal before the District Court and the District Court has enhanced the compensation by granting Rs.2000/- per gunta.

4. The appellant/claimant has preferred the present appeal for seeking further enhancement of compensation on the reason that in the very same village for the very same project the neighboring land owners have been awarded the compensation of Rs.6,000/- per gunta.

Therefore, on this line prays for enhancement of compensation by placing reliance on the judgment of this Court in the case of Smt. Shivamma & others Vs. The Special Land Acquisition Officer in MSA No.135/2021 (LAC) dated 06.02.2023 (Shivamma's Case).

sentences.text:
Learned Additional Government Advocate and also learned counsel Sri. K.S. Bheemaiah,
appearing for the beneficiary justified the order and award passed by the NC: 2024:KHC:44943 District Court and prayed to confirm the same by dismissing the appeal.

6. This Court in Shivamma's Case (supra) has awarded a compensation of Rs.6,000/- per gunta, by observing that in the very same village the lands acquired for the very same project, the District Court has granted a compensation of Rs.6,000/- per gunta and accordingly, accepting the same the claimants in that case were also situated at the same pedestal and granted compensation of Rs.6,000/- per gunta.
7.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Union of India Vs. Balaram and another reported in AIR 2004 SC 3981, has held that it is not fair to make discrimination between the land owners for granting compensation when the purpose of acquisition is for the same project and the lands are identical in nature.

entities.text: Union of India Vs. Balaram and another reported in AIR 2004 SC 3981
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Therefore, this Court in Shivamma's Case (supra) the claimants were awarded compensation of Rs.6,000/- per gunta.
In this case the appellant/claimant's land is situated NC: 2024:KHC:44943 in Kodiyala Village, Gubbi Taluk, Tumakuru District.
Therefore, there could not be any discrimination between the agriculturists, who have lost their land due to acquisition.
Therefore, on the parity in the present case also, the appellant/claimant is entitled compensation of Rs.6,000/- per gunta.
Accordingly, it is awarded.
9. The reference Court has awarded a sum of Rs.1,050/- per gunta.
The same was enhanced by District Court at Rs.2,000/- per gunta.
Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant prays that the District Court, Tumkur, in other cases for the very same project a compensation of Rs.6,000/- was awarded.
Hence, prays to grant compensation on this parity.

This is vehemently opposed by the learned counsel for respondent No.2/beneficiary and submitted that the compensation is determined on the basis of nature of soil, location of the land etc., but there is no evidence by the appellant/claimant in this regard.
Hence, justified the compensation granted by the District Court is correct.
The appellant/claimant shall not be discriminated in this regard when his land is situated in the same place as NC: 2024:KHC:44943 that of other land losers.

Accordingly, in this case also the appellant/claimant is awarded a compensation of Rs.6,000/- per gunta situated at Kodiyala Village,
Gubbi Taluk, Tumakuru District.

10. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.
ii. The market value of the subject land is fixed at Rs.6,000/- per gunta.
iii. The appellant/claimant is entitled all admissible and statutory benefits including interest and costs.
iv. The appellant/claimant is not entitled interest for the delayed period of 965 days in filing the appeal.
